chunks: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ammar ibn Abi al-Ahwas, who said:

I asked Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) about the Sa'iba (unconditionally freed slave), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'Look in the Quran, so whatever was in it, so [the ruling is] the freeing of a slave. So that, O Ammar, is the Sa'iba, for whom there is no guardianship for anyone over her except Allah. So whatever was the guardianship for Allah, it is for His Messenger, and whatever was the guardianship for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), then his guardianship is for the Imam, and his crimes are upon the Imam, and his inheritance is for him.'
ai.seo_question: What is the legal definition and guardianship status of a Sa'iba in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) elucidates the concept of *Sa'iba* by grounding it in the Quranic principle of manumission, establishing a hierarchical chain of *wilayah* (guardianship) that flows from Allah to the Prophet and ultimately to the Imam. This narration is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for affirming the Imam’s exclusive right to inherit the rights of a patron (*mawla*) and to bear criminal liability for the *Sa'iba*, thereby distinguishing the Imam’s authority from that of the Prophet. It underscores the theological continuity of divine guardianship, where the Imam serves as the ultimate inheritor of the Prophet’s rights in the absence of a specific patron.

en.hubeali: Ibn Mahboub, from Ibn Raib, from Ammar Bin Abu Al Ahows who said,

‘I asked Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> about Al-Sa’iba (unconditionally freed slave), so he <sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Look in the Quran, so whatever was in it, so free a slave (accordingly). So that, O Ammar, is the unconditionally freed slave for whom there is no guardian over him except for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>. So whatever was the Guardianship for Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so it is for His<sup>azwj</sup> Rasool<sup>saww</sup>, and whatever was the guardianship for Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup>, so his guardianship is for the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, and his crimes are upon the Imam<sup>asws</sup>, and his inheritance is for him’.
en.sarwar: 2. Ibn Mahbub has narrated from ibn Ri’ab from ‘Ammar ibn abu al-Ahwas who has narrated the following: “I once asked abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about Sa’ibah (unconditionally freed slave).

He (the Imam) said, ‘You must consider what is in the Quran, “setting free a slave” O ‘Ammar, he is Sa’ibah (unconditionally freed slave) over whom there is no guardianship of anyone except Allah. Guardianship over whoever rests with Allah, such guardianship rests with His Messenger; and guardianship over whoever rests with the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, such guardianship rests with the Imam. His liabilities due to his crimes are on the Imam and his legacy is for the Imam.’”
